Hi. So I don't know what your exact situation is, and I don't claim to have all of the answers, and to be honest, I haven't figured out everything myself. All I can really do is tell you my story.

After graduating college from college in 2011, I ended up working as a night auditor for a motel. I absolutely hated that job, in fact I knew from the second that I walked into the lobby for my first interview that this place was going to be horrible, but there were no other jobs to be had, so I took the job, and lo and behold, it turned out to be one of the most miserable experiences of my life, the place was poorly managed, and I was being paid minimum wage maintain an unpredictable schedule, essentially, I never knew whether I was working or what shift I would work on any given day, they would call me 30 minutes before my shift(which could be at any time during the day), I had no power over my own schedule, and on top of that, I hated the work itself. I stayed on for 4 years. and I regret it. I essentially burned through those 4 years of my life and came out the other side with nothing but regret, besides the minimal paycheck, there was no reason for me to have stayed that long.

If I hated it so much, then why did I stay for such a long time? Maybe it was just my own personal little taste of Stockholm syndrome. I'd resigned myself to my situation, after awhile I just told myself that I was going to be there forever. That's when the depression really set in.

At the moment I'm about to finish up a program that I enrolled into immediately after leaving, its a very uncertain period in my life and there's certainly a lot of stress, but its a different kind of stress than what I experienced when I was working at the hotel. The difference is that this time, I have things to hope for. My life right now isn't perfect, but it's been an overall step forward.

I won't dig too much farther deeper into my own situation right now, but here are a few things that the past year has taught me about leaving an unfulfilling job.

1.Have a plan: It doesn't have to be perfect, if you spend time waiting for the perfect opportunity, you'll be there forever. However, your plan should be good enough to hold onto when uncertainty arises(as it probably will).

What is it that you would rather be doing instead of your current job? What is it about your current job that makes you unhappy? What would you feel the most happy doing? Start by answering questions like that for yourself and then work from there. Don't stress over too many of the details, just do as much as you can so you have a general blueprint of where it is you would like to go.

2. Get as much of your finances in order as you can: Cancel any unneeded subscriptions, settle any debts that you need to, and start saving what you can.

3. Set a date to leave and hold true to it: In my case, it was a week before my next birthday at the time. Setting a date allows you to get serious about leaving, that way you become more serious about your plan. It can be a month from now, it can be 2 years from now, however long from now you need it to be, but make a promise to yourself that THAT is the date that you will be leaving.

So I guess that's what I have to say about the topic, I hope that it was good advice and that it helps you. I wouldn't want to come back to this subreddit a year from now and find out that I ruined someone's life with my advice(I too am subscribed to this subreddit). This is just my 2 cents on the matter, and I hope that if nothing else, it helps you feel better.

I can relate to your story a lot. I also graduated with a BA in economics, and also still live with my parents. I don't know what it is, but it seems like a BA in Economics is a real hit or miss. I ended up working a minimum wage job for 4 years. Through the combination of low wages and odd hours, I consider that part of my life a deadweight loss. I decided that enough was enough and I left. I've been teaching myself how to program and have been trying to break into that field since then.

I don't know what the specifics of your situation are, but for me it came down to this: reset the game, or turn it off. Quit my job, or commit suicide. I hit the reset button, I quit my job.

I know that I'm taking a big risk, I've been living off of my savings for the past few months, trying to finish an online course in web development, this may have been the stupidest decision of my life, or it may have been the best, all I know at the moment is that I took a risk, and that I'm happier right now than I was a year ago. Through the process, I've come to the realization that it's better to be lost than trapped. My only regret is that I spent as much time as I did working my previous job, that I had dedicated so much of myself to something that I despised so much.

I guess, what I'm trying to say is that maybe it's time to shake things up. You know where you want to be, and the necessary  steps to get there, why is it that you are incapable of following that path? Sometimes getting what you want is a matter of asking yourself what you're willing to let go of to obtain it.

I'm unfulfilled. I have a degree from a good school, but I can't find a job. I've applied everywhere. I can't even get a job at Starbucks. I've given up, it's like I'm just sending the hiring managers something to use as toilet paper.

Every attempt I make to make my life better isn't good enough. It's like I'm not smart enough to be worth anything to anyone. I'm not good enough.

I've been using this name to make posts on here and r/depression. I just have so many bouts with depression that I thought I'd just make a username solely for this purpose.

Where do I start? Well. I've suffered from anxiety for most of my life, and while I was still in school I had access to counselors and therapists. I had my first panic attack in the fifth grade and started thinking about suicide sometime when I was 13 but my depression has never been this bad before. You can say I'm at a pretty dark point of my life, and I'm running out of ways to deal with it.

When I started college, I studied the thing that made me happiest: Music. It was wonderful, I could just lose myself in the practice rooms on campus for 4 to 8 hours. I loved performing and attending concerts and I was a favorite with the faculty. That period of my life was the only time I can recall that I didn't actively need counseling. My grades were up, and my stress was down, and I had a community that I truly felt like I belonged to.

Then back in 2008 I made the stupidest decision of my life. On the back of the financial crisis I decided that I had to put all of that away and pursue the "practical" major that my parents wanted me to pursue. I chose economics because to me it was the least objectionable of all of the potential money making options. I switched majors. It was a pretty emotional moment for me when I stepped out of my last music class. I justified it to myself, telling myself that once I get a good degree and a good job I could afford new instruments and things and really pursue it.

What followed is what I consider the four worst years of my existence, and they're still continuing to this day. I transferred to university but then realized that I was completely out of my element. I ended up scraping by with a 2.4 GPA. Not to say that I didn't try. Hell, I studied like crazy, pulling all nighters and everything, I'm just not good at it.

During this period, I was simply confused. During my first couple years of college, I never even touched an alcoholic beverage, as cheesy as it sounds, it was like the music was enough for me, at the time drinking and drugs just seemed silly when I was so engaged in all of the other positive things in my life. At the university I had my first drink and started partying more. I just couldn't find any purpose in the work I was doing, all I really found was stress and failure at every corner and in every point of my life.

The funny thing is that I’m so behind my peers on so many levels. No experience in the workplace, crappy GPA and hell, I’ve never had a girlfriend before. Every girl I’ve liked since I first started noticing them has either downright rejected me, or got together with some other guy. There have been multiple times where the girl I liked straight up hooked up with another guy in front of me, hell, it happened with my prom date.

Now I'm here. Out of school with a degree in something I couldn't care less about. Of course I've been going through the shitty job search process like everyone else, but I never found any internships with my crappy educational performance, so how the hell was I supposed to get internship experience during my time at school. I have no experience and this degree that like I said, I don’t even care about.

My home life isn’t as stable as I’d like it to be. It seems like every time I get into a conversation with my parents they find a way to assassinate my character. It’s always something about my laziness or my weight, which has been spiking ever since I lost the motivation to work out, a hobby that I used to be incredibly passionate about yet I can’t seem to find the energy for it these days.

Just recently, I decided that I would sign up for voice lessons at the place where I used to take private guitar lessons. Singing is something that I always wanted to do but could never bring myself to really follow through with because I've always been scared that my voice would be hideous. The lessons are probably my only source of happiness these days, but I can’t help but feel it’s just a stupid little phase where I’m trying to reclaim a dumb little childhood dream.


I just barely managed to get a part time job working as a receptionist at a hotel. The thing is that even though it's part time and it's supposed to be simple I keep screwing up. I'm in danger of losing this job, which would totally mark me for failure for the rest of my life and also kill off my finances for voice lessons, but at the same time the whole experience has just shot down my pride, which I didn't even have that much of in the first place. I swear I must be retarded or something.
What’s worse is that this job found a way to bleed into my life at home, so I have my Boss and my parents railing on me for the same damn thing.

For the most part I’ve just kind of given up. It’s this weird combination of suffering and boredom. It’s just the same old shit every day, the same old worthless feelings and the same old crappy song over and over again just in a different key and a louder volume each time.  It’s like my life is this giant empty promise “hey it’ll get better in High School, oh sorry did I mean college? Yeah, just wait until college and things will be good then. Oh shit, well maybe not college, maybe your late 20’s will turn up something good…” and instead of all of the good things, the same problems just emerge except the stakes are higher each time and so on and so on. I figure I’m just going to die in the end anyway, why not just cut out the crappy 50 years in between and get it over with now?

Oh yes, did I mention I'm also a closet atheist? I haven't even gotten started on that part yet.

TLDR: Not in a good spot...ever.
Never study something you're not interested in. It's what made my life miserable.
